theater: 山東鄒平長白山至章丘臨邑

battle.name: 王薄起義
battle.theater: 山東鄒平長白山至章丘臨邑
battle.brief: 大業七年十月，齊郡鄒平人王薄與同郡孟讓起兵長白山，自號「知世郎」，作《無向遼東浪死歌》號召鄉民拒役，人眾至數萬，幾敗官軍。張須陀率兩萬兵追擊，敗之於泰山下，聯軍十餘萬攻章丘仍潰。後降宇文化及、竇建德、李淵，武德五年死於譚州。卡面的科林斯青銅盔出自西元前七世紀的希臘，只能作對照。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 交戰的兩方是隋朝官軍與齊魯鄉民組成的起義集團。隋朝一方的兵制在文帝朝已經改變：府兵制瓦解，京師禁軍、州郡臨時徵發的鄉兵與按糧餉雇募的募兵並存，另加北方沿邊的蕃騎與降附部眾；平叛的主力則是幾支有經驗的將軍所領的精兵，其中以張須陀部最著名，該部以騎兵搜索、夜襲與追擊見長，能在河北、山東兩地的亂局中獨力維持局面。大業七年秋，隋廷在河北道北端的涿郡、幽州一線集兵百餘萬備征高句麗，山東各縣留下的多是剛從田間抽出的丁壯，既無訓練也無器械；同年秋末雁門被突厥圍困，朝廷又向各郡募兵赴援，齊魯與河北的鄉村再被抽走一層人手與糧秣。起義一方並非國家軍隊，而是以同鄉、姻族、符信與歌謠串連的散眾：核心是鄒平、長白山一帶的鄉民、獵戶、逃戶與拒絕赴遼東的丁壯，王薄與同郡孟讓先起，莊戶爭相歸附，首領之下是數個互不隸屬的小股。河北同期有張金稱、高士達、孫安祖、劉霸道等部，江南有高智慧等部，東西呼應；官軍一分則處處不足，義軍一合則數十萬，這正是隋廷在東北與北方同時用兵時的結構性弱點。
countriesEn: The two sides were the armies of the Sui court and the insurgent groups formed by the peasants of Qi and Lu. The military system on the Sui side had already been changed under Emperor Wen: with the fubing system broken down, the capital guards, the levies hastily raised by each prefecture and county, and soldiers hired against rations existed side by side, together with the tribal horsemen and the surrendered peoples of the northern frontier; the force that actually suppressed the risings was the seasoned troops of a few experienced generals, and the most famous of these was the command of Zhang Xutuo, whose cavalry searching, night attacks and pursuits could hold the line on their own in the disorder of Hebei and Shandong. In the autumn of Daye 7 the court concentrated more than a million men on the Zhuojun and Youzhou line in the north of the Hebei circuit in preparation for the campaign against Goguryeo, and what remained in the counties of Shandong was mostly men taken out of the fields a moment before, without training and without equipment; in the same late autumn, when the Turks besieged Yanmen, the court summoned troops from every commandery to relieve it, and the villages of Qi and Lu and of Hebei lost yet another layer of men and grain. The insurgent side was not a state army at all but a loose public held together by kinship, marriage ties, written talismans and songs: the core was the villagers, hunters, absentees and conscripts who refused to go to Liaodong around Zouping and Mount Changbai. Wang Bo and his fellow townsman Meng Rang rose first, the households of the countryside flocked to them, and beneath the leader there were several mutually independent bands. At the same time there were the bands of Zhang Jincheng, Gao Shida, Sun Anzu and Liu Badao in Hebei and that of Gao Zhihui in Jiangnan, answering one another across the country; the government, divided, was short everywhere, while the insurgents, joined, numbered by the hundred thousand. That was the structural weakness of a court fighting in the north-east and the north at one and the same time.
people: 史籍留下的人名不少，但多數是結局而非戰鬥的細節。王薄是起義的直接首領，齊郡鄒平人，《隋書》只以「河北有民王薄」一句定其身分；大業七年（611）十月，他與同郡孟讓首先起兵反隋，據長白山為根據，自稱「知世郎」，作《無向遼東浪死歌》號召鄉民拒絕出征高句麗，莊戶爭相歸附，一年之間人數增至數萬，曾數度擊敗官軍。孟讓是首義同鄉，其後部眾多併入河北、山東各部。隋將張須陀是決定戰局的人：他以驍勇善戰聞名，率騎兵搜索追擊，先敗王薄於泰山下，追至臨邑再破之，復以兩萬兵馬擊潰王薄與孫宣雅、郝孝德等部聯軍共十餘萬人的攻章丘之役；大業八年（612）他在與宇文化及交戰時中流矢而死，此後又有押解途中病亡的說法——無論何說，河北山東再無能獨當一面的重兵統帥，義軍因此得以再起。《隋書》並記下大業九年山東同時並起的幾股武裝：渤海賊帥格謙自號燕王，孫宣雅自號齊王，各眾十萬；清河賊張金稱眾數萬，同年十一月右候衛將軍馮孝慈討張金稱於清河反為所敗、孝慈戰歿，說明官軍在山東平叛同樣屢敗。竇建德是日後收編河北與山東散卒而成大業者；宇文化及於大業十四年（618）弒煬帝，兵敗聊城，王薄以開城引竇軍之功歸附，旋又改投李淵，受任齊州總管，隨宋州總管盛彥師出兵鎮壓徐圓朗。武德五年（622）三月戊戌，譚州刺史李義滿殺王薄（一說因盛彥師向譚州徵軍糧、李義滿閉倉不與而起釁），其兄子李武意擒殺王薄於譚州，朝廷追究李義滿之死，盛彥師亦獲罪而死。隋煬帝楊廣與三征高句麗是這一切的前提，約在起義之前數月，他仍在涿郡集結大軍。
peopleEn: The histories preserve a fair number of names, though most of them concern how the affair ended rather than how it was fought. Wang Bo was the immediate leader of the rising, a man of Zouping in Qizhou, and the Suishu fixes his identity with a single phrase: there was a man of Hebei named Wang Bo. In the tenth month of Daye 7 (611) he and his fellow townsman Meng Rang rose first in rebellion, took Mount Changbai as their base, styled himself 'the one who knows the age', and composed the Song of Not Going to Liaodong to Die, calling on the countryside to refuse the levies for Goguryeo; the households of the countryside flocked to him, the host grew to several tens of thousands within a year, and several times he beat government troops. Meng Rang was his fellow villager of the first rising, and his bands were later absorbed into the other groups of Hebei and Shandong. The Sui general Zhang Xutuo was the man who decided the battle: famous for dash and skill, he led his cavalry in search and pursuit, beat Wang Bo first under Mount Tai, pursued him to Linyi and broke him again there, and then with twenty thousand men routed the coalition of Wang Bo, Sun Xuanya, Hao Xiaode and the rest, more than a hundred thousand in all, at their attack on Zhangqiu. In Daye 8 (612) he was struck by an arrow and died while fighting Yuwen Huaji, and there is also a report that he fell ill and died on the road under escort; whichever account is right, Hebei and Shandong never again had a heavy commander able to hold a line alone, and the insurgents were able to rise again in consequence. The Suishu also records several armed groups rising at once in Shandong in Daye 9: the bandit chief of Bohai, Ge Qian, styling himself King of Yan, and Sun Xuanya, styling himself King of Qi, each with a hundred thousand men, while the bandit of Qinghe, Zhang Jincheng, had several tens of thousands; in the eleventh month the Right Guard commander Feng Xiaoci attacked Zhang Jincheng at Qinghe, was defeated and was killed, which shows that the government armies were defeated just as often in their own attempts to put down Shandong. Dou Jiande was the man who grew great by absorbing the stragglers of Hebei and Shandong; Yuwen Huaji killed the emperor in Daye 14 (618) and was besieged at Liaocheng, and Wang Bo came over by opening the city to the Dou army, then soon changed sides again to Li Yuan, being appointed chief military commissioner of Qizhou and going out with the Songzhou chief commissioner Sheng Yanshi against Xu Yuanlang. In the third month of Wude 5 (622), on the day wuwu, Li Yiman, the governor of Tanzhou, killed Wang Bo; one account makes it a quarrel that began when Sheng Yanshi called in military grain at Tanzhou and Li Yiman refused to open the granaries. The brother of Li Yiman, Li Wuyi, took and killed Wang Bo at Tanzhou, the court made an inquiry into the death of Li Yiman, and Sheng Yanshi was condemned to die as well. Emperor Yangdi of Sui, Yang Guang, and the three campaigns against Goguryeo stand behind all of this: only a few months before the rising he was still mustering a great army at Zhuojun.
kits: 卡面這件科林斯青銅盔是西元前七世紀希臘的產物：全正面開眼，眼孔與鼻樑連為一體，只留口部與下緣的開口，戴上之後視界極窄，行動與呼吸都受限制；它必須配合密集的方陣才有意義，離了隊形便只剩重量。它與六一一年齊魯的戰場相隔一千二百六十餘年，不可能出現在長白山或章丘，只能當作對照的鏡子：科林斯人的防護靠制度化的方陣，王薄部的防護則是歌謠、符信與同鄉關係——同樣是靠集體秩序換取生存，只是一個有制式裝備，一個沒有。義軍的裝備極為簡陋，多半是農具與獵具改造而成：削尖的竹木長桿、柴刀、耒耜一類的短兵、獵弓與自製箭矢、漁叉，少數骨幹才有從陣亡官軍身上繳來的零散甲片與兜鍪，皮甲只見於個別首領，沒有制式鎧甲，也沒有攻城器械，糧食靠就地取給與劫掠糧倉。隋朝官軍自成體系：明光甲與札甲、披玄甲的重騎兵、步卒所持的槊、長刀與劍，遠程以腰弩、擘張弩與角弓為主，攻取城邑另有雲梯、砲車與水攻之具；馬匹在齊魯向來不缺，郡縣廄牧與北苑牧馬是騎兵行動的基礎。運輸靠牛車、馬車與驛傳，義軍則以人力肩挑與搶來的車輛轉運，一方靠制度，一方靠搶奪。
kitsEn: The Corinthian helmet on the card is a product of seventh-century Greece: the face is open all the way across, the eye openings and the nasal are formed in one piece, and only the mouth and the lower edge are left open, so that once it is worn the field of view is extremely narrow and both movement and breathing are restricted. It makes sense only in company with a dense phalanx; away from the formation it is nothing but weight. It stands about one thousand two hundred and sixty years away from the battlefields of Qi and Lu in 611 and could not have appeared on Mount Changbai or at Zhangqiu, so it can serve only as a mirror for comparison: the Corinthians' protection rested on an institutionalised phalanx, while the protection of Wang Bo's bands rested on songs, talismans and village ties, which is to say both bought survival with collective order, one of them with regulation equipment and the other without. The arms of the insurgents were extremely simple, most of them agricultural and hunting tools turned to other use: sharpened bamboo and wooden poles, wood-axes, short weapons cut from mattocks, hunting bows with home-made arrows, and fish-spears; only a few of the core men had any armour, scattered plates and a helmet taken from government soldiers who had fallen, and leather armour appeared on isolated leaders alone. There were no made-up suits of armour and no siege engines, and food was taken from the spot or seized from granaries. The equipment of the Sui armies formed a system of its own: mingguang and zhajia armour, heavy cavalry wearing black armour, infantry carrying long spears, long sabres and swords, and for the range the waist-mounted crossbow, the shoulder-drawn crossbow and the horn bow, while the taking of walled towns was done with scaling ladders, stone-throwing trebuchots and the use of water. Horses were never scarce in Qi and Lu, and the stallions of the county remounts and of the northern imperial pastures were the basis of the cavalry's movement. Transport was by ox cart, horse cart and the courier relay, whereas the insurgents shifted their loads on human shoulders and on carts they had seized; one side relied on institutions, the other on plunder.
tactics: 起義的戰法只能從結果與當時的條件反推。王薄部的做法大體是鄉民自衛的延伸：以長白山一帶的村社為依託，據山為根據地，平日結伙流動、晝伏夜出，劫掠州郡、糧倉與驛傳，奪糧、奪馬、奪衣物，得手即散，避開官軍搜索的鋒頭；拒絕徵發是他們的訴求，《無向遼東浪死歌》正是這層意思的歌辭，歌與符信同時是聯絡手段，聽得懂那支歌、認得那張符的便是自己人。首起之後人數迅速膨脹，義軍曾數度擊敗官軍，顯示流動作戰在守備空虛的齊魯平原上確實有效；後來引軍南渡、掠魯郡，再北上與孫宣雅、郝孝德等部聯合成十餘萬人攻章丘，失敗的關鍵正在於聯軍：各有首領、互不隸屬、號令不統一、糧秣不繼，兩萬人的精騎得以從容選擇攻擊點，逐部擊破。張須陀部的戰法與此相反：以騎兵搜索、追擊、斷糧為主，晝夜不停地尋找義軍的聚集地，逼迫其不能在同一處久留，遇到大隊則以精騎先衝其首陣、斬將而後亂其眾，義軍在山東丘陵與濟水兩岸之間被追得沒有喘息之機；其戰績之所以突出，靠的是熟悉鄉野地形、馬匹充足與指揮統一，而非器械。這與科林斯青銅盔的邏輯恰好相反：那頂盔要靠隊形才有用，而義軍缺的正是隊形——十餘萬人聚集在一起時，沒有共同的操典與號令，比幾千名散兵更易崩潰。
tacticsEn: The method of the rising can only be reconstructed from its results and from the conditions of the time. The practice of Wang Bo's bands was in effect an extension of village self-defence: they relied on the village communities around Mount Changbai, held the mountain as a base, moved in bands, lay hidden by day and struck by night, plundered commanderies, granaries and the courier relay, took grain, horses and clothing, and broke off as soon as they had it so as to keep away from the point of the government's search. Their demand was refusal of the levies, and the Song of Not Going to Liaodong to Die gave voice to exactly that; the song and the talismans were at once the means of liaison, for whoever knew the song and recognised the paper was one of them. After the first rising the host swelled quickly, the insurgents beat government troops several times, and it was plain that mobile warfare did work on the plain of Qi and Lu while the garrisons were thin. Later they led the host south across the river and raided Lujun, and then, having joined with the bands of Sun Xuanya, Hao Xiaode and others to make more than a hundred thousand men, attacked Zhangqiu. The key to that failure was the coalition itself: each group had its own leader, none was subordinate to another, the orders did not run from one centre, and the grain did not follow, so that twenty thousand cavalry could choose where and when to strike and break the host part by part. The method of Zhang Xutuo was the opposite: cavalry searching, pursuing and cutting the supplies, never ceasing the hunt for the place where the insurgents had gathered, so that they could never stay long in one place; against a large body he struck the leading ranks first with picked horse, cut down the commanders and then broke the rest, and the insurgents were chased across the hills of Shandong and the banks of the Ji without a moment to breathe. What made his record what it was was his knowledge of the country, the number of horses under him and the unity of his command, not his weapons. The logic is the exact opposite of the Corinthian helmet: that helmet is useful only with a formation, and what Wang Bo's army lacked was a formation, for when a hundred thousand men are gathered together without common drill or common orders they break more easily than a few thousand scattered men.
data: 可核實的數字大致如下。時間軸：大業七年（611）十月起兵，據長白山；一年之間人數增至數萬，曾數度破官軍；大業八年（612）前後在泰山下、臨邑連敗於張須陀，與孫宣雅、郝孝德等部合眾十餘萬再攻章丘，仍為張須陀所破，其時張須陀率兩萬兵馬。《隋書·煬帝紀下》記大業九年（613）冬十月：「齊人孟讓、王薄等眾十餘萬，據長白山，攻剽諸郡，清河賊張金稱眾數萬，渤海賊帥格謙自號燕王，孫宣雅自號齊王，眾各十萬，山東苦之。」此後王薄輾轉於宇文化及、竇建德、李淵之間，武德二年（619）降宇文化及，開聊城引竇軍入城，武德五年（622）三月戊戌為譚州刺史李義滿所殺。背景數字方面，第一次征高句麗「天下兵百餘萬，長子供食、官給作者」，翌年正月宇文述等率三十萬五千人渡河，說明隋朝把兵力的重心壓在東北，山東的守備必然空虛；同年秋末雁門被突厥圍困，朝廷詔天下募兵赴援，齊魯郡縣再出一層力。地理上，長白山在齊魯境內，舊籍與今人注釋所指不一，通常繫於今山東鄒平長白鎮一帶，另有說繫於章丘境內；齊郡鄒平距濟南府城約百餘里，泰山、臨邑、章丘與鄒平同在齊魯平原的數百里之間，一日之內可達數縣，義軍與官軍的接觸因此極其頻繁。本役的雙方死傷數字沒有可靠記載：《隋書》與《資治通鑑》只留下「眾至數萬」「破之」「潰散」一類的結果性記載，各將領傳中「斬首數千級」「擒獲數萬」一類數字屢見，但沒有任何一條明確屬於王薄之役，不可套用。
dataEn: The figures that can be established are roughly these. The time axis: the rising began in the tenth month of Daye 7 (611), based on Mount Changbai; within a year the host had grown to several tens of thousands and several times defeated government troops; around Daye 8 (612) it was beaten by Zhang Xutuo under Mount Tai and again at Linyi, and the coalition of Wang Bo with the bands of Sun Xuanya, Hao Xiaode and the rest, more than a hundred thousand men, was broken by Zhang Xutuo at its attack on Zhangqiu, Zhang Xutuo commanding twenty thousand horse and foot. The Suishu, in the annals of Emperor Yangdi, records for the tenth month of Daye 9 (613) that 'the men of Qi, Meng Rang, Wang Bo and the rest, more than a hundred thousand, held Mount Changbai and raided the commanderies; the bandit of Qinghe, Zhang Jincheng, had several tens of thousands; the bandit chief of Bohai, Ge Qian, styled himself King of Yan, and Sun Xuanya styled himself King of Qi, each with a hundred thousand men; Shandong suffered from it.' After that Wang Bo passed between Yuwen Huaji, Dou Jiande and Li Yuan: in Wude 2 (619) he went over to Yuwen Huaji and opened Liaocheng to the Dou army, and in the third month of Wude 5 (622), on the day wuwu, he was killed by Li Yiman, the governor of Tanzhou. Among the background figures: for the first campaign against Goguryeo, 'more than a million men were mustered from throughout the realm, with the emperor providing the food and the government the artisans'; in the first month of the following year Yuwen Shu and the others led thirty and five thousand men across the river; both show that the Sui had thrown the weight of its manpower to the north-east, so that the defence of Shandong was necessarily hollow. In the same late autumn the Turks besieged Yanmen and the court summoned troops from every commandery, so the counties of Qi and Lu gave out one more layer of men. Geographically, Mount Changbai lies within the Qi and Lu country, and the old records and modern notes disagree about its position, most associating it with the Changbai town of present-day Zouping in Shandong and some with the territory of Zhangqiu; Qizhou's Zouping is about a hundred li from the city of Jinan, and Mount Tai, Linyi, Zhangqiu and Zouping all lie within a few hundred li of one another on the plain of Qi and Lu, so that several counties lay within a day's march and the insurgents and the government troops were in contact very often. Reliable figures for the losses on both sides do not exist: the Suishu and the Comprehensive Mirror preserve only result-of-battle statements of the kind 'the host reached several tens of thousands', 'he was broken' and 'it scattered', while the biographies of neighbouring commanders repeatedly give figures like 'several thousand heads cut off' and 'tens of thousands captured'; not one of these is expressly attached to Wang Bo's rising and none may be borrowed for it.
cause: 起義的成因可以分成遠近兩層。遠的一層是隋朝自文帝末年以來積累的社會負擔：租調之外雜斂日重，力役與兵役同時加在丁身之上，修河、造龍舟、營建東都與洛陽、巡行天下，一次次把役夫與車馬抽空鄉村；大業年間三巡江都、兩幸北塞，沿途供億，地方不堪其擾。更深的一層是兵制變化帶來的後果：文帝朝把府兵改為募兵，農民一旦離籍當兵便失去土地與生產，州縣的鄉兵只具名額而無訓練，國家常備的精兵又遠在邊鎮與京師之間，地方守備只剩空架子。近的一層非常具體：大業七年是第一次征高句麗的徵發年，隋廷在涿郡、幽州一線集兵百餘萬，山東、河北正是最近的徵兵區與糧源區，役夫、戰馬與糧秣沿河北道北運，鄉村丁壯大量被抽走，農事失管；同年秋末雁門被圍，朝廷又向各郡募兵解圍；入冬前齊魯一線已聚了大量拒絕赴遼東的丁壯。在這樣的局面下，民間對三征高句麗的不滿早已流傳，王薄與孟讓以一支《無向遼東浪死歌》把「寧死也不去遼東」的怨望變成集合的口號，起義因此得以成立：歌辭不是修飾，而是這場戰爭真正的動因與武器。
causeEn: The causes of the rising can be divided into a near and a far layer. The far layer is the weight the Sui had been accumulating since the end of Emperor Wen's reign: exactions grew heavier alongside the regular levies and taxes, labour and military service fell at the same time upon the able-bodied, and the digging of channels, the building of the great ships, the construction of the eastern and western capitals and the tours of the realm drained villages of porters, wagons and draught animals one time after another; through the Daye years the emperor toured the south three times and the northern frontier twice, and the immense provisioning of the route left the localities unable to bear it. Deeper still are the consequences of the change in the military system: under Emperor Wen the fubing had been replaced by hired troops, so that a peasant who left his register to serve lost both his land and his means of production; the county levies existed as quotas without training, and the state's seasoned soldiers stood far off at the frontier and in the capital, so that local defence was left with nothing but hollow shells. The near layer is very concrete: Daye 7 was the year of the great levy for the first campaign against Goguryeo. The court mustered more than a million men on the Zhuojun and Youzhou line, and Shandong and Hebei, the nearest districts of recruitment and of supply, supplied the porters, the war horses and the grain that went north along the Hebei circuit, so that huge numbers of village men were taken away and the fields went untended; in the same late autumn the siege of Yanmen brought yet another levy, summoned from every commandery to relieve it; and before the winter closed there were already gathered on the Qi and Lu line large numbers of conscripts who refused to go to Liaodong. Under such conditions the resentment of the countryside over the three campaigns against Goguryeo had long been spreading, and Wang Bo and Meng Rang turned it into a password for assembly with a single song, the Song of Not Going to Liaodong to Die: rather than ornament, the words of the song were the true motive and the true weapon of this war.
impact: 王薄起義的意義，首先在於它把隋末亂世的時間線定了下來。此後的史書把大業七年視為民變的起點之一：王薄在齊魯、張金稱與高士達在河北、孫安祖、劉霸道與竇建德在河北、江南有高智慧等部，幾處同時燃起，而原先互不相干的鄉民一旦有了歌號與符信作為聯絡手段，響應的速度便快得多；到大業九年，起事已遍及二十餘州，隋廷對每一處都要分兵，而分兵正是它兵力不足的根源；《隋書》在同一年的記載裡說山東同時並起數股各眾十萬的武裝，一句「山東苦之」，正是正統史家對這個地區的判斷。制度上的後果同樣深遠：為鎮壓各地起義，隋朝把兵權進一步收到州郡與行軍總管之手，以募兵與鎮守代替已廢的府兵，地方上大量出現以首領為核心的私屬部曲，國家的軍隊與豪強的部眾界線日漸模糊；唐承隋制而不得不改用募兵、倚重方鎮，河北與山東的尚武之風與藩鎮割據的雛形，都可以在隋末這一代的鄉民起義裡找到源頭。另一層影響在人物的結局上：王薄先降宇文化及、再開聊城引竇建德入城、又投李淵為齊州總管，示範了起義首領被各方收編、反覆轉手的那條路；竇建德、李淵與王薄之間的這些交易，最後都收束在唐的統一裡，而隋朝在山東河北的秩序則再也沒有重建起來。文獻上，《無向遼東浪死歌》與王薄自號「知世郎」的記錄，被後世視為隋唐民間歌辭中最早的起義歌之一，標誌著亂世之中民間自己的聲音開始被記錄、被流傳。
impactEn: The significance of Wang Bo's rising lies first of all in the fact that it set the timeline of the chaos at the end of the Sui. The histories written afterwards treat Daye 7 as one of the starting points of the rebellions: Wang Bo in Qi and Lu, Zhang Jincheng and Gao Shida in Hebei, Sun Anzu, Liu Badao and Dou Jiande in Hebei, Gao Zhihui and the rest in Jiangnan, several places alight at once, and once villagers who had had no connexion with one another possessed songs, passwords and talismans by which to keep in touch, the speed of the answering rose sharply; by Daye 9 the risings covered more than twenty commanderies, and the court had to divide its troops to meet every one of them, and that division of troops was precisely the root of its shortage; the Suishu entry for the same year names several armed groups in Shandong at once with a hundred thousand men each, and the four characters 'Shandong suffered from it' are the orthodox historian's own judgement on that region. The institutional consequences ran deep as well: to put down the risings in every quarter the Sui drew military authority further into the hands of the commanderies and the mobile commanders, replacing the defunct fubing with hired soldiers and with garrison duty, while in the localities private bands gathered around leaders multiplied, and the line between the armies of the state and the dependants of the powerful grew ever blurrier. The Tang inherited the Sui institutions but had to rely much more heavily on hired soldiers and on the regional commands, and the martial temper of Hebei and Shandong and the embryo of the separatist military governors can both be traced back to the peasant risings of the last Sui generation. A second layer of the effect is visible in the fate of the leading men: Wang Bo first went over to Yuwen Huaji, then opened Liaocheng to Dou Jiande, then went over to Li Yuan as chief military commissioner of Qizhou, and in doing so he demonstrated the road along which insurgent leaders were taken in, handed over and passed from hand to hand. Those transactions between Dou Jiande, Li Yuan and Wang Bo were all finally drawn up into the unity of the Tang, while the Sui order in Shandong and Hebei was never rebuilt. In the literature, the Song of Not Going to Liaodong to Die and the record of Wang Bo's styling himself 'the one who knows the age' came to be regarded as one of the earliest recorded rising songs of the popular literature of the Sui and Tang, and they mark the point at which the voice of the common people in a time of disorder began to be written down and passed on.
result: 就起義本身而言，結果是兩層。其一是一場由義軍自己造成、又由義軍自己失去的失敗：王薄的隊伍在一年之間確實壯大到數萬人，也確實數度擊敗過官軍，但義軍終究是流動的散眾，沒有穩定的根據地、沒有可延續的編制、沒有能供給十餘萬人的糧秣；大業八年，張須陀以精騎搜尋追擊，先敗之於泰山下，再追至臨邑，復以兩萬兵馬擊潰其與孫宣雅、郝孝德等部的十餘萬聯軍於章丘，主力自此瓦解，餘眾散歸各部或歸入竇建德等新起的武裝。其二是王薄個人的結局，他比自己的起義活得更久，也走得更遠：武德二年（619）他降於弒君的宇文化及，在竇建德兵圍聊城時開城引軍入城，隨後又轉投李淵，受任齊州總管，隨宋州總管盛彥師出兵鎮壓徐圓朗；武德五年（622）三月戊戌，他為譚州刺史李義滿所殺（一說因盛彥師向譚州徵軍糧、義滿閉倉不與而起釁），其兄子李武意在譚州擒殺他，朝廷追究李義滿之死，盛彥師也獲罪而死。卡面上的科林斯青銅盔放在這裡恰好合適：那是西元前七世紀的希臘工藝，全正面開眼，戴它的人只能靠隊形活；六一一年齊魯的起義者沒有盔，卻有歌與同鄉的關係，同樣是一種群體的防護。差別只在於，隋朝在張須陀死後已經沒有制度能夠把這樣的隊伍編入任何編制之中。
resultEn: As for the rising itself, the outcome has two layers. The first is a failure the insurgents built themselves and then lost themselves: Wang Bo's force did indeed grow to several tens of thousands within a year and did indeed beat government troops several times, but it remained in the end a mobile and scattered multitude, with no stable base, no organisation that could be carried forward, and no means of feeding a hundred thousand men. In Daye 8 Zhang Xutuo searched and pursued with picked horse, beat them first under Mount Tai, pursued them to Linyi, and then with twenty thousand men broke the coalition of more than a hundred thousand made up of Wang Bo with the bands of Sun Xuanya, Hao Xiaode and the rest at Zhangqiu. The main body came apart there, and the survivors dispersed back to the various groups or went over to the new armed forces of Dou Jiande and others. The second layer is Wang Bo's own end: he lived longer than his rising and went further. In Wude 2 (619) he went over to Yuwen Huaji, who had killed the emperor, and when Dou Jiande besieged Liaocheng he opened the city and brought the army in; he then changed sides again to Li Yuan, was made chief military commissioner of Qizhou, and went out with the Songzhou chief commissioner Sheng Yanshi against Xu Yuanlang. In the third month of Wude 5 (622), on the day wuwu, he was killed by Li Yiman, the governor of Tanzhou, one account making it a quarrel that began when Sheng Yanshi called in military grain at Tanzhou and Li Yiman closed the granaries against him; Li Wuyi, the brother of Li Yiman, took him and killed him at Tanzhou, the court made an inquiry into the death of Li Yiman, and Sheng Yanshi was condemned as well. The Corinthian helmet on the card fits the moment exactly: it is seventh-century Greek work, the face open all the way across, and the man who wears it can only live by his formation. The rebels of Qi and Lu in 611 had no helmet, but they had a song and the ties of the same village, which is a form of collective protection just the same. The only difference is that after Zhang Xutuo's death the Sui no longer had institutions that could enrol such a company into any order of battle at all.
